class="docs-check is-disabled"><input type="checkbox" disabled=""/><span>Include what I just ran<span class="docs-check-hint"> (run a demo or a code block first)</span></span></label><pre class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Package one routine of this repository as a Muse Code project skill and run it headless in CI. Create .agents/skills/&lt;id&gt;/SKILL.md for the routine I name (default: drafting release notes from merged changes), validate it with `muse skills validate`, and add a CI job that runs `muse exec --json --disable-approval --max-model-steps 40` with that skill, keeps the JSONL output as a build artifact, and gates on the repo&#x27;s own tests.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Extending and automating&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Project skills: &lt;repo&gt;/.agents/skills/&lt;skill-id&gt;/SKILL.md. Commands: muse skills validate, install, enable, list, inspect, and `muse skills import --from claude|codex`.
- muse exec exit codes: 0 the turn completed (not proof the work is right), 1 failed or cancelled (including --max-model-steps), 2 usage error, 130 or 143 on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
- Headless runs can&#x27;t answer prompts: --disable-approval keeps the sandbox; --yolo drops it and trusts the workspace. Linux runners need a working bubblewrap and a non-musl build.
- Resume and audit: `muse exec --session-id &lt;uuid&gt; &quot;Continue the task.&quot;` and `muse export --session &lt;uuid&gt; --out run.json`.
- Hooks (.muse/hooks.json, the settings hooks block, managed_hooks_path) and MCP tools run outside the sandbox. mcp_servers entries take transport stdio (command, args, env) or streamable_http (url, headers).

Starter code (Python)
import subprocess
import sys

# CI: keep the JSONL events, then let the tests decide (exit 0 only means the turn ended).
with open(&quot;muse-run.jsonl&quot;, &quot;w&quot;) as out:
    run = subprocess.run(
        [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--json&quot;, &quot;--disable-approval&quot;, &quot;--max-model-steps&quot;, &quot;40&quot;, &quot;Use the release-notes skill.&quot;],
        stdout=out,
    )
codes = {1: &quot;failed or cancelled&quot;, 2: &quot;usage error&quot;, 130: &quot;SIGINT&quot;, 143: &quot;SIGTERM&quot;}
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec: {codes.get(run.returncode, run.returncode)}&quot;)
subprocess.run([&quot;npm&quot;, &quot;test&quot;], check=True)

Done when
- `muse skills validate ./.agents/skills/&lt;id&gt;` passes.
- The CI job&#x27;s test step decides pass or fail, and the --json output is saved as an artifact.
- The key comes from META_API_KEY or a stored sign-in and never appears in code, logs or commits.</pre><div class="docs-prompt-foot"><span class="docs-prompt-count">2,970<!-- --> stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M6 9.5l6 6 6-6"></path></svg></button><div id="_R_95av5spfklb_" class="docs-toc-panel" hidden=""></div></nav></div><p class="docs-p">Take Muse Code past a single interactive session: distribute work across parallel agents, package reusable workflows as skills, wire your own commands into the lifecycle with hooks, connect external tools through MCP, and run the agent non-interactively in CI.</p><p class="docs-p">For structured orchestration with parallel groups, dependent stages, monitoring, and reusable JavaScript definitions, see <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows">workflows</a>. To coordinate independent live sessions, use <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/session-messaging">session messaging</a>.</p><h2 id="multi-agent" class="docs-h docs-h2">Subagents and multi-agent<a class="docs-anchor" href="#multi-agent" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Distribute a large job across a team of agents that work in parallel, and steer them from one place. A lead session spawns child agents, hands each a bounded task, and keeps managing the group while they run.</p><p class="docs-p">A <strong>subagent</strong> is a child agent that the lead spawns for one bounded task. Children share the lead&#x27;s checkout unless the lead requests worktree isolation for that child. Ask for isolated worktrees when parallel children may write, and keep read-only children in the shared checkout.</p><p class="docs-p">An isolated child gets a Muse Code-managed Git worktree. The request can be rejected when the current profile, workspace, provider, or Git state cannot support isolation. It never silently falls back to the shared checkout.</p><p class="docs-p">The <code class="docs-code-inline">--subagent-worktree-isolation</code> launch flag remains accepted for compatibility. It does not force every child into a worktree; isolation is still selected per child.</p><p class="docs-p">Use subagents when a job splits into tasks that are each bounded, independently verifiable, and would otherwise contend for the same files. Keep the work on one agent when the steps are strictly sequential.</p><p class="docs-p"><strong>Steer the agents.</strong> Run <code class="docs-code-inline">/subagents</code> to view running and past subagents. Run <code class="docs-code-inline">/tasks</code> to manage direct subagent tasks and use the actions available for the selected row. The lead also manages children through its native subagent tools.</p><p class="docs-p">A few properties worth knowing:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>One agent tree can execute eight agents at once by default, including the root agent. Set <code class="docs-code-inline">agents.execution_capacity</code> from 1 through 64 in <code class="docs-code-inline">settings.json</code> to change the limit. An unconfigured <code class="docs-code-inline">ultra</code> root uses 64.</span></li><li><span>A spawn attempted when the tree is full is rejected. An accepted child can still wait for a host scheduler slot before it starts.</span></li><li><span>Children can spawn grandchildren. Every descendant shares the same root-tree capacity.</span></li><li><span>Cancellation is cooperative: a cancelled child that never reaches a checkpoint keeps running, and one mid-write finishes that write.</span></li><li><span>The runtime journals every spawn, status change, and control action, so you can answer &quot;which child did what, and when&quot; after the run. A child commits changes only when its task explicitly asks it to.</span></li></ul><h3 id="observer-agents" class="docs-h docs-h3">Background observer agents<a class="docs-anchor" href="#observer-agents" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">Alongside the main session, Muse Code runs a team of background observer agents. Each one watches a single axis of quality, and can insert a short advisory into the main agent&#x27;s next turn without an interruption. An observer never answers for you: it proposes, a reconciler decides, and only an accepted proposal reaches the main agent.</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Memory recall</strong>: surface a note from local project <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#local-memory">memory</a> relevant to the next reply.</span></li><li><span><strong>Skill recall</strong>: surface a project <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#skills">skill</a> the task should load first.</span></li><li><span><strong>Goal tracking</strong>: hold the agent to a declared <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#goals-loops">goal</a> and decline to close the turn until the work is done.</span></li><li><span><strong>Verification</strong>: check that the agent ran the work it claims it finished.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">All four observers, including verification, are on by default. Rollout gates and your <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings file</a> can still disable them.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Observers add token usage</p><p class="docs-p">Each enabled observer makes its own model calls, so the default set of four adds token usage in addition to the main session.</p></div></div><h2 id="skills" class="docs-h docs-h2">Skills<a class="docs-anchor" href="#skills" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">A skill packages a repeatable workflow the agent can load on demand: a set of instructions, and optionally tools and files, that turn &quot;explain how we do X&quot; into a single invocation. Muse Code ships built-in skills, and you can add your own or import them from other agents.</p><p class="docs-p">Skills load from four sources:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Built-in</strong>: skills that ship with Muse Code.</span></li><li><span><strong>User</strong>: your account-wide skills in <code class="docs-code-inline">$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/skills</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">~/.agents/skills</code>, available in every project. Muse Code also discovers <code class="docs-code-inline">~/.claude/skills</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">$CODEX_HOME/skills</code> by default, falling back to <code class="docs-code-inline">~/.codex/skills</code> when <code class="docs-code-inline">CODEX_HOME</code> is unset. A user preference and rollout gate can disable these foreign personal skill roots.</span></li><li><span><strong>Project</strong>: skills committed to a repo under <code class="docs-code-inline">&lt;repo&gt;/.agents/skills/&lt;skill-id&gt;/SKILL.md</code>, shared with anyone who clones it. Muse Code also scans repo-local <code class="docs-code-inline">.codex/skills</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">.claude/skills</code>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Plugin</strong>: skills contributed by enabled plugin bundles.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Manage and invoke skills:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> list</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">                    # every skill, all sources</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> inspect</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skill-i</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">d</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> enable</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skill-i</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">d</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --scope</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> project</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> install</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> ./my-skill</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --scope</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> user</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> validate</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> ./my-skill</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">     # check it before installing</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">skills</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> import</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --from</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> claude</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">    # or: --from codex</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">In an interactive session, invoke a skill with its slash shortcut. Built-in skills include <code class="docs-code-inline">/plan</code> (turn a task into a grounded, decision-complete plan, then stop for approval), <code class="docs-code-inline">/grill</code> (stress-test a plan or design before you build, recording each settled decision and a written scope contract in your project docs), <code class="docs-code-inline">/taste</code> (a design-quality gate for frontend work), and <code class="docs-code-inline">/threejs</code> (references for building Three.js scenes). The agent can also load a relevant skill when a <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/extending#observer-agents">background observer</a> surfaces one.</p><p class="docs-p">The bundled <code class="docs-code-inline">migrate</code> skill imports your Claude Code or Codex memory notes and MCP servers into Muse Code. Invoke it with <code class="docs-code-inline">/migrate</code>. It complements <code class="docs-code-inline">muse skills import</code>, which brings in skills from those agents.</p><h2 id="hooks" class="docs-h docs-h2">Hooks<a class="docs-anchor" href="#hooks" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Wire your own shell commands into Muse Code&#x27;s lifecycle. A hook binds a shell command to a lifecycle event. When the event fires, Muse Code runs the command and acts on its result: enforce a check, format code, or block an action before it happens, without a change to the agent itself.</p><p class="docs-p">Hooks come from three sources:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong>Project</strong>: committed to the repo at <code class="docs-code-inline">&lt;project-root&gt;/.muse/hooks.json</code>.</span></li><li><span><strong>User</strong>: your machine-wide hooks, defined in your <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings</a>.</span></li><li><span><strong>Managed</strong>: a file that the <code class="docs-code-inline">managed_hooks_path</code> setting points to, for centrally administered hooks.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Project hooks run only after you trust the project folder. User hooks run from your own settings without a separate hook-level trust step. Managed hooks also run without a project-trust step, so whoever controls the managed hooks file controls what executes.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-warning" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M8.6 2.8a1.6 1.6 0 0 1 2.8 0l6.9 12a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4 2.4H3.1a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4-2.4l6.9-12z"></path><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 6.8h1.8l-.2 5.2H9.3z M10 13.2a1 1 0 1 1 0 2 1 1 0 0 1 0-2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">Hooks run outside the sandbox</p><p class="docs-p">Only add hooks whose commands you&#x27;ve read. A hook&#x27;s command runs directly through your shell, <strong>outside</strong> the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions">sandbox and approval</a> that govern the agent&#x27;s own tools. The only hardening is a cleared environment with a small allowlist.</p></div></div><h3 id="hook-events" class="docs-h docs-h3">Lifecycle events<a class="docs-anchor" href="#hook-events" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">A hook binds to exactly one event. The available events are <code class="docs-code-inline">SessionStart</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">UserPromptSubmit</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PreToolUse</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PermissionRequest</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolUse</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolUseFailure</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolBatch</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PreLLMCall</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PostLLMCall</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PreCompact</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">PostCompact</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">SubagentStart</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">SubagentStop</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">Notification</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">Stop</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">StopFailure</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">SessionEnd</code>. <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolUseFailure</code> runs when a tool call fails or crashes. <code class="docs-code-inline">PostToolBatch</code> runs once after each committed batch of tool calls and receives them in order; it can block the batch with a reason, stop the turn, or add context. <code class="docs-code-inline">StopFailure</code> runs once when a turn ends in a final model failure, and receives the failure category and safe details. <code class="docs-code-inline">Notification</code> fires when the agent needs your approval, so a hook can alert you. <code class="docs-code-inline">SessionEnd</code> runs during orderly session termination. It is observational: its output cannot block termination, inject context for a later request, or stop the session.</p><p class="docs-p">Muse Code discovers and validates hooks at session startup. A malformed project or managed hook file contributes no handlers from that source and produces a startup warning. A malformed user settings file fails settings validation. Unsupported events, matchers, or handlers skip the affected entry and produce a source-specific warning.</p><p class="docs-p">There is no active <code class="docs-code-inline">muse hooks</code> command family or per-hook trust command. Fix the reported configuration and start a new session to reload it.</p><h2 id="mcp" class="docs-h docs-h2">MCP servers<a class="docs-anchor" href="#mcp" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Connect external tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Declare servers in the <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp_servers</code> block of your <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings file</a>. Each server takes a <code class="docs-code-inline">transport</code>: either <code class="docs-code-inline">stdio</code> (with <code class="docs-code-inline">command</code>, <code class="docs-code-inline">args</code>, and <code class="docs-code-inline">env</code>) or <code class="docs-code-inline">streamable_http</code> (with <code class="docs-code-inline">url</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">headers</code>). Every server also takes <code class="docs-code-inline">enabled</code> and <code class="docs-code-inline">mode</code>. For <code class="docs-code-inline">stdio</code>, the optional <code class="docs-code-inline">framing</code> setting controls message framing. A non-default <code class="docs-code-inline">framing</code> value on <code class="docs-code-inline">streamable_http</code> fails validation.</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">json</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="json" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">{</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-property)"> "mcp_servers"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">:</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-property)">    "my-tools"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">:</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> {</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-property)"> "transport"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">:</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "stdio"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">,</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-property)"> "command"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">:</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "my-mcp-server"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">,</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-property)"> "args"</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">:</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> []</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)">}</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-punct)"> }</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">A server&#x27;s <code class="docs-code-inline">mode</code> defaults to <code class="docs-code-inline">required</code>. If a required server fails to start, the whole run aborts. Set <code class="docs-code-inline">mode</code> to <code class="docs-code-inline">optional</code> for a server that Muse Code should skip with a warning when it&#x27;s unavailable.</p><p class="docs-p">Server configs support <code class="docs-code-inline">${VAR}</code> environment-variable interpolation, and Muse Code passes <code class="docs-code-inline">MUSE_SESSION_ID</code> to <code class="docs-code-inline">stdio</code> servers. A tool whose server declares it read-only runs without an approval prompt under <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#approval-modes">on-request approvals</a>. Run <code class="docs-code-inline">/mcp</code> in an interactive session to see a live inventory of connected servers and their tools.</p><p class="docs-p">A named toolset (<code class="docs-code-inline">run.toolset</code>) can select MCP tools by their full name, such as <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp__docs__search</code>, or with a trailing <code class="docs-code-inline">*</code>: <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp__docs__*</code> selects every tool from the <code class="docs-code-inline">docs</code> server, and <code class="docs-code-inline">mcp__docs__search*</code> selects its tools whose names start with <code class="docs-code-inline">search</code>. If a selected MCP tool is still missing after the MCP servers start, the run stops before contacting the model and lists every missing name.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-warning" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path fill="currentColor" d="M8.6 2.8a1.6 1.6 0 0 1 2.8 0l6.9 12a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4 2.4H3.1a1.6 1.6 0 0 1-1.4-2.4l6.9-12z"></path><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 6.8h1.8l-.2 5.2H9.3z M10 13.2a1 1 0 1 1 0 2 1 1 0 0 1 0-2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">MCP tools aren&#x27;t sandboxed</p><p class="docs-p">Only connect servers you trust. <strong>MCP tools are not sandboxed.</strong> Unlike shell commands, an MCP server runs as an ordinary child process (stdio) or a direct network connection, outside the filesystem and network <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#sandbox">sandbox</a>. Approval still applies, but containment does not.</p></div></div><h3 id="mcp-oauth" class="docs-h docs-h3">Sign in to remote MCP servers<a class="docs-anchor" href="#mcp-oauth" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h3><p class="docs-p">A remote server can require an OAuth 2.1 sign-in. Authenticate in the browser or headless, and Muse Code keeps and refreshes the tokens for you:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">mcp</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> login</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">serve</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">r</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">mcp</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> logout</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">serve</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">r</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">A sign-in done in another terminal is picked up without a restart, and a startup or mid-session 401 tells you the exact <code class="docs-code-inline">muse mcp login</code> command to run. To turn off automatic client registration, set <code class="docs-code-inline">&quot;mcp_oauth_dynamic_client_registration&quot;: false</code> in your <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration#settings-file">settings file</a>.</p><h2 id="headless" class="docs-h docs-h2">Headless and CI<a class="docs-anchor" href="#headless" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><p class="docs-p">Run Muse Code without a terminal UI. <code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> takes one prompt, runs it to completion, and exits, so you can drive the agent from a script, a job, or a CI pipeline:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">exec</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "Update the changelog for the latest release and run the tests."</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">exec</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --prompt-file</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> ./task.txt</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">exec</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --json</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "Refactor the auth module and run the tests."</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-comment)">   # JSONL events on stdout</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p"><code class="docs-code-inline">muse exec</code> prints the agent&#x27;s output to stdout and returns a process exit code that reflects <strong>how the run ended, not whether the work is correct</strong>: <code class="docs-code-inline">0</code> when the turn completes, <code class="docs-code-inline">1</code> when it fails or is cancelled (including a <code class="docs-code-inline">--max-model-steps</code> limit), <code class="docs-code-inline">2</code> for a usage error, and <code class="docs-code-inline">130</code> or <code class="docs-code-inline">143</code> on SIGINT or SIGTERM. An agent can finish its turn (exit <code class="docs-code-inline">0</code>) and still report failing tests, so gate on your own test command, not on the exit code alone.</p><p class="docs-p"><strong>Control approvals for automation.</strong> A non-interactive run has no one to answer an approval prompt, so choose a posture in advance:</p><ul class="docs-list"><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--disable-approval</code></strong>: skip approval prompts, but keep the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#sandbox">sandbox</a> on to contain what runs.</span></li><li><span><strong><code class="docs-code-inline">--yolo</code></strong>: disable approval and the sandbox for a fully unattended run. It also trusts the workspace, so use it only on trusted code in a disposable, isolated container. See <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#run-without-guardrails">run without guardrails</a>.</span></li></ul><p class="docs-p">Cap a run&#x27;s work with <code class="docs-code-inline">--max-model-steps</code> so a stuck task can&#x27;t loop indefinitely.</p><div class="docs-callout docs-callout-note" role="note"><span class="docs-callout-icon"><svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8.5" fill="currentColor"></circle><path fill="#fff" d="M9.1 8.6h1.8v5.6H9.1z M10 5.3a1.1 1.1 0 1 1 0 2.2 1.1 1.1 0 0 1 0-2.2z"></path></svg></span><div class="docs-callout-body"><p class="docs-callout-title">CI sandbox requirements</p><p class="docs-p">The <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions#sandbox">sandbox</a> must be able to run on the CI runner, which on Linux needs a working bubblewrap and a non-musl build. Without it, every sandboxed shell command aborts as an environment failure.</p></div></div><p class="docs-p"><strong>Resume and audit non-interactively.</strong> Headless runs are <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/interactive#session-model">sessions</a> like any other. To continue an interrupted job non-interactively, use <code class="docs-code-inline">exec</code> with the session id. <code class="docs-code-inline">muse resume</code> opens the interactive UI and is not a headless surface:</p><div class="docs-code"><div class="docs-code-head"><span class="docs-code-label">bash</span><span class="docs-code-tools"><button type="button" class="docs-copy-btn" aria-label="Copy code" title="Copy code"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9 9h10.5v10.5H9z M15 9V5.5A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 13.5 4h-8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 4 5.5v8A1.5 1.5 0 0 0 5.5 15H9"></path></svg><span class="sr-only" aria-live="polite"></span></button></span></div><div role="group" aria-label="bash" class="docs-code-body"><pre class="shiki docs" style="background-color:transparent;color:var(--docs-syn-fg)" tabindex="0"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">exec</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --session-id</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">uui</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">d</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-string)"> "Continue the task."</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">muse </span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">export</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --session</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)"> &#x3C;</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">uui</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)">d</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-operator)">></span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> --out</span><span style="color:var(--docs-syn-fg)"> run.json</span></span></code></pre></div></div><p class="docs-p">Muse Code refuses a workspace mismatch unless you pass <code class="docs-code-inline">--allow-workspace-switch</code>. The export document embeds the CLI version that produced it, so pin the version if you gate on its hash.</p><h2 id="next-steps" class="docs-h docs-h2">Next steps<a class="docs-anchor" href="#next-steps" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">#</a></h2><ul class="docs-list"><li><span>Keep the whole team inside the same <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/permissions">permissions and sandbox boundary</a>.</span></li><li><span>Build repeatable multi-agent runs with <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/workflows">workflows</a>.</span></li><li><span>Give skills and subagents the project facts they rely on in <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration">configuration and context</a>.</span></li><li><span>Connect external agent tooling to the model from the <a class="docs-link" href="/docs/coding-agents">coding agents</a> guide.</span></li></ul><nav class="docs-pager" aria-label="Previous and next page"><a class="docs-pager-link" rel="prev" href="/docs/muse-code/configuration"><span class="docs-pager-dir"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M14.5 6l-6 6 6 6"></path></svg>Previous</span><span class="docs-pager-title">Configuration and context</span></a><a class="docs-pager-link is-next" rel="next" href="/docs/muse-code/changelog"><span class="docs-pager-dir">Next<svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M9.5 6l6 6-6 6"></path></svg></span><span class="docs-pager-title">Changelog</span></a></nav><p class="docs-credit">Mirrored from<!-- --> <a href="https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">dev.meta.ai/docs/<!-- -->muse-code/extending</a> <!-- -->(synced <!-- -->Oct 30, 2026<!-- -->). class="docs-prompt-preview" aria-label="Prompt preview" tabindex="0">You&#x27;re Claude Code, working in my repository.

Task
Package one routine of this repository as a Muse Code project skill and run it headless in CI. Create .agents/skills/&lt;id&gt;/SKILL.md for the routine I name (default: drafting release notes from merged changes), validate it with `muse skills validate`, and add a CI job that runs `muse exec --json --disable-approval --max-model-steps 40` with that skill, keeps the JSONL output as a build artifact, and gates on the repo&#x27;s own tests.

Read this first
Meta&#x27;s docs page &quot;Extending and automating&quot; as Markdown: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending.md
It&#x27;s the source of truth for request and response shapes. The same page for people: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending

Setup
- Muse Code: muse on PATH (install: curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | sh, or irm https://dev.meta.ai/install.ps1 | iex on Windows; check: muse --version). Its default model is muse-spark-1.2; --model picks another.
- Auth: muse reads META_API_KEY from the environment (in CI, from the secret store), else a key stored with muse auth set or a browser sign-in; not MODEL_API_KEY. Never hard-code, print or commit the key.
- Python: a plain script that runs muse through subprocess where a step needs it.

Facts to get right
- Project skills: &lt;repo&gt;/.agents/skills/&lt;skill-id&gt;/SKILL.md. Commands: muse skills validate, install, enable, list, inspect, and `muse skills import --from claude|codex`.
- muse exec exit codes: 0 the turn completed (not proof the work is right), 1 failed or cancelled (including --max-model-steps), 2 usage error, 130 or 143 on SIGINT or SIGTERM.
- Headless runs can&#x27;t answer prompts: --disable-approval keeps the sandbox; --yolo drops it and trusts the workspace. Linux runners need a working bubblewrap and a non-musl build.
- Resume and audit: `muse exec --session-id &lt;uuid&gt; &quot;Continue the task.&quot;` and `muse export --session &lt;uuid&gt; --out run.json`.
- Hooks (.muse/hooks.json, the settings hooks block, managed_hooks_path) and MCP tools run outside the sandbox. mcp_servers entries take transport stdio (command, args, env) or streamable_http (url, headers).

Starter code (Python)
import subprocess
import sys

# CI: keep the JSONL events, then let the tests decide (exit 0 only means the turn ended).
with open(&quot;muse-run.jsonl&quot;, &quot;w&quot;) as out:
    run = subprocess.run(
        [&quot;muse&quot;, &quot;exec&quot;, &quot;--json&quot;, &quot;--disable-approval&quot;, &quot;--max-model-steps&quot;, &quot;40&quot;, &quot;Use the release-notes skill.&quot;],
        stdout=out,
    )
codes = {1: &quot;failed or cancelled&quot;, 2: &quot;usage error&quot;, 130: &quot;SIGINT&quot;, 143: &quot;SIGTERM&quot;}
if run.returncode != 0:
    sys.exit(f&quot;muse exec: {codes.get(run.returncode, run.returncode)}&quot;)
subprocess.run([&quot;npm&quot;, &quot;test&quot;], check=True)

Done when
- `muse skills validate ./.agents/skills/&lt;id&gt;` passes.
- The CI job&#x27;s test step decides pass or fail, and the --json output is saved as an artifact.
